Redis vs Valkey Differences

Historical Context and Shift
Analyzing the evolution of memory-based data stores following the early 2024 licensing change, where the core technology transitioned from a traditional open-source BSD model to dual source-available licensing. This shift triggered the creation of an open-source fork under the Linux Foundation, heavily supported by major cloud vendors and enterprise infrastructure leaders.
Architectural and Ecosystem Divergence
Synthesizing key operational differences between the engines, particularly in multi-threading execution architectures, memory optimization strategies, native module integration versus plugin extensions, and managed cloud platform adoption across primary infrastructure providers.
Targeted Information Gathering
Planning initial targeted searches to gather recent technical benchmarks, licensing nuances, ecosystem support metrics, and feature developments across both project roadmaps to pinpoint the three most critical distinctions.

Shift in Open Source Dynamics
I am observing a major evolution in the in-memory data store ecosystem following the transition from permissive open-source licensing to source-available models. The establishment of Valkey under neutral Linux Foundation governance has consolidated backing from major infrastructure providers and enterprise contributors, creating a distinct dual-track ecosystem.
